name: Drive Letter and Volume Name
location: Windows XP: SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USBSTOR (find the device's ParentIdPrefix), then correlate that value against SYSTEM\MountedDevices to find the last mount point. Windows 7+: SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Portable Devices\Devices; SYSTEM\MountedDevices (examine \DosDevices\<letter> values for a matching device serial number); SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Search\VolumeInfoCache.
purpose: Discovers the last drive letter and volume name assigned to a specific USB device the last time it was connected to the system.
key_fields: USBSTOR ParentIdPrefix (Windows XP) - links a USBSTOR device entry to its MountedDevices record
MountedDevices \DosDevices\<letter> values - binary data containing a device serial number or volume GUID to match against a known device
SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Portable Devices\Devices subkeys (Windows 7+) - named for the device, storing the last friendly volume/device label
VolumeInfoCache entries (Windows 7+) - cached volume label and related metadata keyed by volume
normal_baseline: A stable, small set of drive-letter assignments for known recurring devices, with volume names matching each device's manufacturer default or a user-assigned label the analyst can independently confirm.
anomalies: A drive letter reassigned between clearly unrelated devices in a short window, breaking the expected one-device-per-letter continuity an analyst would otherwise expect
A volume name that doesn't match a device's previously documented label, suggesting the media was relabeled/reformatted to blend in or to impersonate another known device
MountedDevices \DosDevices value manually deleted or edited, breaking the letter-to-serial-number correlation for a device otherwise evidenced elsewhere (usb-device-history, setupapi-devlog)
VolumeInfoCache or Windows Portable Devices entries present with no corresponding USBSTOR/MountedDevices record, indicating partial artifact deletion
anti_forensic_notes: These keys are overwritten on each new mount, so only the LAST drive-letter/volume-name mapping for a device is recoverable here - deleting or editing the relevant MountedDevices value removes that mapping with no lower-level history retained in these locations; connection history itself must come from usb-device-history's registry timestamps or setupapi-devlog.
interpretation: Only the last USB device mapped to a specific drive letter can be identified from these keys - historical drive-letter assignments over time are not retained here. Cross-reference the recovered volume name and letter against shell-item data in LNK files and shellbags to place the device in a broader activity timeline.
